newsitem.title: USA: Cold spell forecast for U.S. Plains wheat areas.
newsitem.headline: Cold spell forecast for U.S. Plains wheat areas.

text.p: Frigid weather was forecast this weekend for the central and southern Plains, but meteorologists doubt the cold will be a threat to the hard red winter wheat crop.
"I think we need it to be a bit colder than this to cause any problems (to the wheat)," said Joel Burgio, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp.

Forecasts call for single-digit Fahrenheit temperatures late Friday and Saturday across Nebraska, Iowa and northern Kansas. Single-digit to mid-teens were likely from central Kansas to northern Oklahoma.
In northern Texas, lows could range from the mid-teens to the upper 20s Fahrenheit.
"We are looking at some real cold temperatures Saturday morning," said Fred Gesser, Weather Express Inc.

As of Monday, March 10, five percent of Kansas wheat had started spring growth and 19 percent of Oklahoma's had broken dormancy and started growing, according to agricultural statistics services in those states.
An official in the Oklahoma Agricultural Statistics Service office said it was probably too early in the growing season for the pending cold spell to significantly damage the wheat.
A moderate warmup was likely next week, with temperatures fluctuating from above normal Monday and Tuesday to below normal Wednesday and Thursday, the meteorologists said.
